app.title: NoOBS

sources.btMicWarn: Warning: while this Bluetooth microphone is connected and NoOBS is open (even without selecting it to record — the level meters already open access to the mic), Windows keeps the headset in the HFP profile. The device's audio quality drops to mono 8 or 16 kHz and the volume usually goes to maximum. Bluetooth Classic limitation — unchecking here won't fix it. To restore HD, disable or disconnect the device in Windows, or use a separate USB microphone.
sources.btSpeakerWarn: Warning: Bluetooth speaker. When any app on Windows accesses a Bluetooth microphone (including NoOBS's level meters), this device automatically drops to phone-call quality (mono 8 or 16 kHz) and maximum volume. Bluetooth Classic limitation — for HD, disable the Bluetooth microphone in Windows, or use BT LE Audio (newer hardware + Windows 11).

export.title: Export recording
export.regionsHint: The chosen regions are placed side by side, with no empty gap where one was left out. Picking a monitor here clears the crop drawn on the preview — they are two ways of saying the same thing, and the last gesture wins.
export.resolutionHint: Lowering the resolution shrinks the file the most. We never scale above the original.

scaleHint.bicubic: Sharpest on fine detail, and the slowest of the three. It is the default because it is the safe middle ground for any content.
scaleHint.bilinear: About 1.8× faster than bicubic, with a slightly softer image. A good pick when speed matters more than detail.
scaleHint.area: Averages the discarded pixels: the fastest, and the one that aliases least on big reductions (4K → 720p, for instance). On small reductions it looks slightly softer than bicubic.

export.qualityHint: {{band}} The scale runs from 0 (lossless) to 51 (worst). The bitrate is variable (VBR): the encoder spends whatever the content needs, so the final size depends on the video.
export.containerHintMp4: MP4 opens in any player, site or phone. Saved to the recordings folder.
export.containerHintMkv: MKV is the app's native format and handles HEVC/AV1 fine, but not every player or site accepts it. Saved to the recordings folder.
export.rangeHint: Drag on the bar to move the cursor; use the mouse wheel over it (or Ctrl + + / Ctrl + −) to zoom in and hit the exact second. "Split here" cuts at the cursor; "Remove split" undoes the nearest split (highlighted in red); "Drop segment" removes the segment under the cursor from the final video. Kept segments are joined in order, with no gap.
export.needOnePart: At least one segment must be included in the final video.
export.previewUnavailable: Preview unavailable for this codec — exporting still works.
export.zoomIn: Zoom in (Ctrl + +, or mouse wheel over the bar)
export.zoomOut: Zoom out (Ctrl + −, or mouse wheel over the bar)
export.removeCutAt: Removes the split at {{at}} (joins both segments)
export.fpsHint: Fewer frames per second make the file smaller and the export faster, at the cost of smoothness. Above 60 fps the size gain is small: neighbouring frames are nearly identical and cost little.
export.cropHint: Drag the edges of the preview to crop; drag the middle of the frame to reposition. Ctrl + mouse wheel zooms in (or the − and + buttons above). Once zoomed, drag with the middle mouse button — or Shift + left button — to pan and reach the rest of the image.
export.cropOf: Cropped to {{w}}×{{h}}, from {{sw}}×{{sh}} of the source

reset.label: Restore defaults
reset.hint: Resets ALL tabs to the factory defaults, not just this one. Applied immediately.

language.label: Language
language.hint: Language of the NoOBS interface. "Automatic" uses the Windows language; other values force the selected language.

windowTitle.label: Window title
windowTitle.hint: Name shown in the title bar, the taskbar button and the tray icon. Leave blank to use "NoOBS".

filename.label: Output file name
filename.hint: Use codes in braces: {AAAA} year, {MM} month, {DD} day, {HH} hour, {NN} minute, {SS} second, {ZZZ} millisecond. Everything else is literal text.

codec.label: Video codec
codec.swWarn: Encodes on the CPU and uses every core. Above 1080p it may not keep up with the recording and drop frames. Prefer a hardware encoder if your GPU has one.
codec.hint: Automatic picks the best available option in the order H.264 hardware → H.264 software → AV1 hardware → HEVC hardware. Only choose manually if you know what you're doing.

hotkey.label: Global hotkey to start/stop recording
hotkey.hint: Check the desired modifiers (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Win) and pick a main key. Examples: Pause or Ctrl+Shift+G.
hotkey.noKey: No hotkey set. Pick a main key (and optionally modifiers) to enable the global hotkey.
hotkey.activeHint: Current hotkey: {{spec}}. Uncheck all modifiers and pick Not set to disable.
hotkey.invalidSpec: Invalid hotkey — pick at least one main key (letter, number, F1-F12, Pause, etc).

hint.0: Maximum compression — tiny files, very low quality.
hint.1: Extreme compression — very small files, clearly visible loss.
hint.2: Very high compression — small files, noticeably reduced quality.
hint.3: High compression — much smaller files, visibly below normal.
hint.4: Moderate compression — smaller files, slight loss of sharpness.
hint.5: Default — balanced between file size and visual quality.
hint.6: Good quality — slightly larger files, cleaner image.
hint.7: High quality — larger files, sharper video.
hint.8: Very high quality — much larger files, loss hard to notice.
hint.9: Extremely high quality — large files, virtually no visible loss.
hint.10: Maximum quality — huge files, beyond what the eye can tell apart.

hint.low: {{fps}} fps — low framerate, motion may look choppy. Smaller files.
hint.smooth: {{fps}} fps — smooth, standard video rate. Compact files.
hint.good: {{fps}} fps — good fluidity, great for general use.
hint.high: {{fps}} fps — high fluidity, ideal for games and fast motion.
hint.veryHigh: {{fps}} fps — very high fluidity. Larger files.

hint.precise: Every {{sec}} second — very precise cuts when splitting in the player. Slightly larger file.
hint.balanced: Every {{sec}} seconds — good balance between cut points and size. (Recommended)
hint.medium: Every {{sec}} seconds — slightly smaller file; less precise cuts.
hint.spaced: Every {{sec}} seconds — smaller file; splitting may drift well off the chosen point.

library.label: Library previews and duration

hint.auto: Generates preview and duration only for videos available on this PC; skips cloud-only files (OneDrive) so they aren't downloaded.
hint.always: Generates preview and duration for every video, downloading from the cloud if needed.
hint.off: Doesn't generate preview or duration for existing videos — only for new recordings made in NoOBS.

library.cloudNote: Your recordings folder appears to be on OneDrive.

autostart.label: Start with Windows
autostart.hint: NoOBS launches automatically when you log into Windows.

closeToTray.label: Minimize to tray
closeToTray.hint: Lets NoOBS use the system tray icon. With this option enabled, the window's X button sends to tray instead of quitting — click the icon to reopen, or use the icon's menu to actually quit.

minimizeOnRecord.labelTray: Minimize to tray when recording starts
minimizeOnRecord.hintTray: When a recording starts, the NoOBS window is sent to the system tray — useful for recording the screen without the app's own window appearing in the video. The global hotkey still works to stop.
minimizeOnRecord.hintTaskbar: When a recording starts, the NoOBS window is minimized — useful for recording the screen without the app's own window appearing in the video. The global hotkey still works to stop.

notifyOnRecord.label: Show Windows notification on record start/stop
notifyOnRecord.hint: Shows a Windows notification when a recording starts or finishes. Only useful when the window is automatically minimized — otherwise the recording state is already visible in the window.

recIndicator.label: Show a recording indicator on screen
recIndicator.hint: Shows a red dot with the elapsed recording time in a corner of the primary monitor. You see the indicator, but it doesn't appear in the recording (it's excluded from capture). Requires Windows 10 2004+.

playSound.label: Play start/stop recording sound
playSound.hint: Plays a short two-note sequence when starting (ascending) and stopping (descending) a recording — discreet audible confirmation.

stopOnLock.label: Stop recording when computer is locked
stopOnLock.hint: When you lock Windows (Win+L, switch user, or automatic lock), the ongoing recording is finalized — avoids accidentally recording long sessions when you step away.

hibernate.label: Free memory after 1 minute in tray
hibernate.hint: When the app stays in the tray for over 1 minute without recording, releases all resources and stays at ~5 MB of RAM. Only available with 'Minimize to tray' enabled.

autoRecord.label: Automatically record during calls
autoRecord.hint: Starts recording when it detects the microphone being used by another app (a Teams, WhatsApp, etc. call) and stops when it's released. Works even with the window in the tray or the app hibernating.
autoRecord.appsHint: Apps to watch, comma-separated (part of the process name). Empty = any app that uses the microphone. Browser calls show up as chrome.exe / msedge.exe.
autoRecord.exceptHint: Exceptions: apps to ignore even when they use the microphone (comma-separated). Since you're watching every app, these stay out.
autoRecord.devicesHint: Choose which devices are included when recording starts on its own from a call — a selection of its own, separate from the home screen. All start checked; only the ones hidden in the Devices menu are left out.
autoRecord.devicesEmpty: No devices available. Check the Devices menu.

buttons.resetTitle: Restore all fields to their default values (applied instantly)

updates.autoHint: Checks the GitHub releases page once a day, from 6 AM onwards, in the background. Nothing is downloaded or installed — just a notice when a new version exists.
updates.upToDate: You are on the latest version.
updates.failed: Could not check right now. Check your connection and try again.

muteWhenDeviceMuted.label: Silence the track while the microphone is muted in Windows
muteWhenDeviceMuted.hint: While the microphone is muted in Windows, its track is recorded as silence. This covers the mute button on your headset, the system mute, and call apps that tell Windows when you mute. A mute done only inside the app, without telling Windows, cannot be detected — in those cases the microphone keeps being recorded.

transcribe.hostHint: Address and port of the Transcritor API container. The routes are fixed (/jobs and /health) — only the host is configurable.
transcribe.pendingCloud: {{count}} recording(s) left out: they are cloud-only. Transcribing would download them, so the batch skips them — open a recording to download it, or transcribe one at a time from its menu.
transcribe.queueHint: One transcription at a time — the container itself serializes requests, so queuing more would not help. The percentage comes from the API and is real: it measures how much audio has been transcribed, and it advances in jumps because processing happens in 30-second windows.

stage.waitingInstall: waiting for the local engine to be installed

language.label: Transcription language
language.hint: Setting the language keeps the transcription from coming out translated: when detecting on its own, the transcriber decides from the start of the audio and, when it gets it wrong — silence, music, noise — writes everything in the wrong language.

onStop.label: Transcribe automatically when a recording ends
onStop.hint: The recording joins the queue as soon as it ends. If the server is down it waits, and the queue is saved — it carries on after closing the app or restarting the computer.

engine.label: Where to transcribe
engine.local: On this computer, using the graphics card
engine.server: On a server (Docker or another computer)
engine.hint: On this computer it is faster and times each word more precisely, but it does not tell speakers apart — when recording with isolated tracks, the speaker still comes from the device name. The server (Transcritor API) separates speakers.

local.missing: The local engine is not installed yet.
local.missingHow: The download is about {{size}} (the audio.cpp engine and the Qwen3 models) and happens only once. It needs a graphics card with a Vulkan driver — AMD, NVIDIA or Intel. No Docker, nothing else to install.
local.resumeHint: If the connection drops or you cancel, what was already downloaded is kept and the download resumes where it stopped.
local.readyCpu: Ready — transcribing on the CPU. No graphics card with Vulkan was found, so it will be much slower.
local.readyHow: Uses {{size}} in %LOCALAPPDATA%\NoOBS\asr. The engine only runs while there is something in the queue and frees the video memory a few minutes later.
local.removeBusy: The local engine cannot be removed while installing or transcribing.

replay.label: Memory buffer
replay.hint: With the buffer on (button on the main screen), NoOBS keeps the last few minutes of the screen in memory, without writing to disk. When something worth keeping happens, press the shortcut: the clip becomes a regular recording and the buffer starts over empty — saving again brings only what came after, with about a second repeated at the seam so nothing is lost between clips.
replay.autoStart: Turn the buffer on when NoOBS opens
replay.autoStartHint: When checked, the buffer starts keeping footage by itself every time NoOBS opens. When unchecked, the button on the main screen turns the buffer on only until the app closes.
replay.intoRecording: Record from what the buffer has kept
replay.intoRecordingHint: When checked, starting a recording with the buffer on reuses what it has already kept: the file starts with that footage and continues without a break. When unchecked, whatever was in the buffer is discarded and the recording starts from scratch.
replay.apps: Turn on by itself with these programs
replay.appsPlaceholder: e.g.: valorant, cs2, League of Legends
replay.appsHint: Program names separated by commas. While any of them is open the buffer turns on by itself; when they all close, it turns off. Part of the name is enough ("valorant" matches "VALORANT-Win64-Shipping"). Works with NoOBS hibernating too. Empty = off.
replay.indicator: Show the buffer indicator on screen
replay.indicatorHint: A green dot with how much is kept, in the corner of the screen. You see it but it does not enter the recording, and clicking it saves the clip. Requires Windows 10 2004+.
replay.memoryHint: Whichever runs out first wins: the buffer drops the oldest part once it exceeds the time OR the memory. A still screen takes a few MB per minute; a 4K 120 fps game at maximum quality reaches ~1.5 GB per minute. The maximum in the list is what fits on this machine, always leaving 4 GB of RAM free.
replay.hotkeyHint: Only active while the buffer is on — when it's off, the combination goes back to other programs.

devices.hint: Uncheck to hide a device from the main screen. Hidden devices don't show in the list and aren't recorded.

about.title: About NoOBS
about.tagline: Lightweight screen recorder with OBS Studio embedded
about.intro1: NoOBS was born out of frustration with the complexity of OBS Studio — configuring scenes, sources and devices for every recording.
about.intro2: The idea here is simplicity: open, click Record, you're recording. Displays, webcam, microphones and system audio are detected and ready automatically.
about.intro3: Lightweight, fast, intuitive — a premium product designed so your recording always just works.
features: Ready in one click — screens, webcam, microphones and system audio detected automatically, with no scenes or sources to set up
Separate audio tracks — the mic and each output become their own track in the MKV
GPU acceleration: AV1, HEVC, H.264 (NVIDIA / AMD / Intel) with CPU x264 fallback
Quick editing in the player — split, merge, waveform and per-track volume
Automatic recording during calls — detects the microphone in use by Teams, WhatsApp and the like, and stops on its own
Global shortcut and hibernation mode (~5 MB of RAM when idle in the tray)
MKV container — the recording survives a power loss
builtWith: libobs (OBS Studio core) — recording, encoder and capture
FFmpeg — remux, track extraction and thumbnails
about.footer: Free software based on OBS Studio (GPL v2+), FFmpeg (LGPL/GPL) and Microsoft's WebView2.

error.cantChangeSourcesWhileRecording: Can't change video sources while recording.
error.exportBusy: An export is already running. Wait for it to finish or cancel it.
error.exportWhileRecording: Can't export while recording — encoding would fight the recording for CPU and GPU. Stop the recording and try again.
error.exportBadRange: Invalid range. Pick a start before the end.
error.exportNoSpace: Not enough disk space to export. About {{needed}} free is needed, but only {{free}} is available. Free up space and try again.
error.exportNoEncoder: Could not open the selected encoder. Try H.264 — software (x264), which works on any machine.
error.exportFailed: Could not export this recording. Check the log for details.
